subject: Planting 16, 579
fact: The date is Planting 16, 579, when Zephyr sits for breakfast and waits for the arrival of Calmer and the man-at-arms promised by Ranos Davl.

subject: Zephyr
fact: Zephyr is short, 5’2”, has copper-red hair, hazel eyes, and a flattish nose, and exhibits the over-eager look of religious zealots.
source_quote: Zephyr scrutinizes him. He is short, 5’2”, has copper-red hair, hazel eyes, and a flattish nose. He also has that over-eager look that religious zealots have.

subject: Calmer
fact: Calmer’s armor is polished and his holy symbol, the cudgel, dangles from his wrist; he is insecure about this being his first adventure.
source_quote: Calmer arrives first, his armor polished and his holy symbol, the cudgel dangling from his wrist. Calmer is a bit insecure about this being his first adventure.

subject: Thorne
fact: Thorne is a rugged man in his late 30s with a weathered face marked by scars from past skirmishes, brown hair cropped short, piercing green eyes hidden beneath a weather-beaten leather cap, and is called Duke because his name sounds like a throne.
source_quote: My name is Thorne. My friends call me Duke because my name sounds like a throne. Zephyr takes stock of Thorne or Duke. He is a rugged man in his late 30s with a weathered face marked by a few scars from past skirmishes. His brown hair is cropped short, and his piercing green eyes are hidden beneath the brim of a weather-beaten leather cap.

subject: Zinia
fact: Zinia is the masked one who has been watching Zephyr and their two new companions, noticing nothing amiss, and suggests heading to the Moathouse.
source_quote: The masked one had been watching Zephyr and their two new companions, trying to see if anything was off. He noticed nothing. He suggests that they head to the Moathouse since all that they needed to do had been done.

subject: Moathouse
fact: The Moathouse is surrounded by a scrub of thorns, thistles, weeds, and shrubs along the track leading to the ruins; the track is mostly overgrown, cluttered with fallen branches and trees, washed out in places, mired in others, and the land sinks and becomes boggy near the entrance; tall marsh plants grow thickly where cattails and tamaracks do not; the bogs stink; the vegetation appears dense and prolific but sickly and unhealthy; creepers and vines throw their strangling loops over the skeletons of dead saplings and living bushes alike; the rushes and cattails rustle and bend even to a slight zephyr; weird birdcalls, croakings, and other unwholesome sounds come faintly across the fen; a side path, banked high to cross over the wetland, leads just north to the entrance of the ruin; the track is only about 15 feet wide with crumbling embankments making travel near the edge dangerous.
source_quote: A scrub of thorns, thistles, weeds, and shrubs grows thickly along the edge of the track leading to the ruins. Even the track is mostly overgrown and cluttered with fallen branches and trees. Here and there, it is washed out, in other places a mire. Some game evidently still follows the pathway, however, for after a mile or sofaint traces can be seen. But even considering this, going is slow, and it takes over an hour to reach the place on horseback, or two to trudge along on foot. Considerable hacking and clearing is necessary to make the way passable, so double the time required for the first trip. After two miles, as the track turns more northerly, the land begins to sink and become boggy. Tall marsh plants grow thickly where cattails and tamaracks do not. Off to the left can be seen the jagged silhouette of the moathouse. A side path, banked high to cross over the wetland to either side, just north to the entrance of the ruin. The track here is only about 15 feet wide or so, with crumbling embankments making travel near the edge dangerous. The bogs stink. The vegetation appears dense and prolific, but somehow sickly and unhealthy, creepers and vines throwing their strangling loops over the skeletons of dead saplings and living bushes alike. The rushes and cattails rustle and bend even to a slight zephyr, and weird birdcalls, croakings, and other unwholesome sounds come faintly across the fen.

subject: Moathouse courtyard
fact: Past the door of the Moathouse is a large courtyard, and to the northeast are stairs leading to the house portion; the doors at the top of the staircase are broken; one is flat on the floor, and the other is sundered.
source_quote: Past the door is a large courtyard, and to the northeast are some stairs. The stairs lead to the house portion of the moathouse. The doors at the top of the staircase are broken; one is flat on the floor, and the other is sundered.

subject: Moathouse great hall
fact: The great hall was once a great audience chamber, as shown by the tattered banners and tapestries on the walls, destroyed furniture, and heaps of rotting cloth thrown into corners; once richly appointed, it has been thoroughly searched, sacked, and despoiled; leaves and dirt cover the floor, and cobwebs hang from walls and the ceiling above; pieces of beams and chunks of stone poke through, indicating the upper stories are totally destroyed and likely impassable to anything larger than a rat; to the east and south are passageways, and to the northeast is a door.
source_quote: Past the door is a great hall. This was once a great audience chamber, as shown by the tattered banners and tapestries on the walls, destroyed furniture, and heaps of rotting cloth thrown into corners. Once richly appointed, it has been thoroughly searched, sacked, and despoiled. Leaves and dirt cover the floor, and cobwebs hang from walls and the ceiling above. Looking up, he sees that pieces of beams and chunks of stone poke through, indicating that the upper stories of the place are totally destroyed and likely to be impassable to anything larger than a rat. To the east and south are passageways, and to the northeast is a door.

subject: flat river rock
fact: A flat river rock is inscribed with an eye and a tear, found by Sequoia in the Moathouse great hall.
source_quote: Out of the corner of Sequoia’s eye, he sees a flat river rock inscribed with an eye and a tear.

subject: Voss
fact: Voss is a bandit who explains he became a bandit due to gambling debts, drinking, and being forced to sell his property; he was working for the Temple and was given the symbol of the eye and tear; he cries hysterically when confronted with the Church of St. Cuthbert’s punishment for cult membership.
source_quote: The bandit, whose name is Voss, starts crying even more. Sequoia is baffled, and Calmer explains that membership in the cult is punishable by death. Under questioning, the bandit explains that he didn’t want to be a bandit, but there was this property that he had to sell, then there were the gambling debts and the drinking, and well, it just went downhill from there. He explains, “The Moathouse was a good hideout because nobody wanted to come here anymore. The Temple was dead, and adventurers picked this place clean, so nobody came here.” “You were working for the Temple,” Sequoia explains coldly and flatly.

subject: giant frogs attack
fact: Four giant frogs jump out of the pool near the drawbridge and attack; they catch Zinia flatfooted but miss him; later, four more frogs jump onto the bridge, causing it to shatter; Sequoia and Calmer fall into the water; two frogs are injured; one frog chomps at Calmer and is knocked to death’s door; Zinia kills one frog in the water; Zephyr kills another frog; an arrow through the eye kills the last frog.
source_quote: Four giant frogs jump out of the pool near the bridge and attack. Although they catch the Zinia flatfooted, they miss him. When he has a chance to absorb the tactical situation, he sees that all the frogs missed. “The last ribbit,” he thinks. A few seconds later, the ground is drenched in the blood of giant frogs. Four more giant frogs jump onto the bridge. The frogs' and the party's weight causes the bridge to shatter. Zinia doesn’t fall in, but Sequoia and Calmer do. He looks around and sees Zephyr still standing on the bridge. Sequoia and Calmer have been injured from the falling debris, but so have two frogs. A frog chomps at Calmer and is knocked to death’s door. Zinia jumps into the water and strikes and kills one of the injured Frogs. From behind him, he hears another frog croak. It’s last. It is dead at Zephyr's hand. When Zinia stands up, he sees the last frog is also dead from an arrow that went through the eye and into the amphibian’s skull.

subject: bandit ambush and interrogation
fact: Zephyr uses an illusion to get bandits to open the door; Zephyr, Zinia, and Sequoia sneak in one at a time; Zephyr kills the leader and indicates seven more left; Zinia kills one quietly; Sequoia kills two bandits; three bandits escape through an enlarged arrow slit; Sequoia kills one more and blocks the exit; Zinia knocks out the last bandit; Voss is interrogated and reveals he was given the symbol by his boss; Calmer’s explanation of St. Cuthbert’s punishments terrifies Voss; Sequoia comforts him and learns the symbol meant belonging.
source_quote: A sudden bang is heard in the room just outside the door. “Zephyr has used an illusion to get the folks inside to open the door for us,” thinks Sequoia. The door opens, and a man in scruffy, dirty clothes with yellowing teeth peers through. He then retreats into the door, and there is muttering. Sequoia can’t understand what they are saying. The two rogues and the monk co-ordinate with hand gestures. They will sneak into the room one at a time, attack, and retreat. Sequoia waits as Zephyr enters. He hears a body fall to the ground. As Zephyr exits, he indicates seven more left and that the leader is dead. Sequoia waits as Zinia enters. The satisfying sound of a body hitting the ground quietly precedes Zinia’s return. The rogue sneaks in the past through the door and sees the bandit leader dead on the ground, pooling in blood in the middle of the room. To his left is another dead bandit. Sequoia kills one with his shortswords and then leaves the chamber. The bandits recover from the shock of the surprise attack and start screaming that they have to get out of there. Three of the bandits escape to the south through an arrow slit that has been enlarged to allow easy retreat. Sequoia kills one more of the bandits and then stands in front of the exit, blocking it. He turns to Zinia, “Keep him alive. We want to interrogate him.” Zinia knocks him out with a flurry of blows. Voss then starts to cry hysterically and in panic. Calmer offers to help, but apparently, Calmer’s idea of calming a man terrified of being killed by an Evil Cult is to explain to him what the Church of St. Cuthbert does to its enemies. Sequoia pushes the cleric away and sits down next to Voss. He says, “Look, I know you are just a desperate man caught up in something bigger than themselves. And I really don’t need to hand you over to the authorities. I just need to know what this symbol is.” Voss looks at him, “It’s what the big boss gave the boss who gave it to us. It meant we belonged.”

subject: Church of St. Cuthbert
fact: The Church of St. Cuthbert punishes membership in the Temple with death; Calmer is a cleric of St. Cuthbert who believes in leading and guarding the rear; he expresses glee when he says, “I think it’s important that we call to calm down,” which is unintentionally ironic.
source_quote: Calmer explains that membership in the cult is punishable by death. Calmer shouts, “No. We have come here to do a job and will do it.” Calmer says, “I think it’s important that we call to calm down.” The rogue stares at the cleric, wondering if that was intentional; the cleric's obvious glee makes it clear that it was.

subject: drawbridge to Moathouse
fact: The drawbridge to the Moathouse is made of rotting wood; when the four giant frogs jump onto it, its weight causes it to shatter; Sequoia and Calmer fall into the water below; Zephyr remains standing on the bridge.
source_quote: At the last moment, the masked spy notices the bridge rotting. He’s about to shout when four more giant frogs jump onto the bridge. The frogs' and the party's weight causes the bridge to shatter. Zinia doesn’t fall in, but Sequoia and Calmer do. He looks around and sees Zephyr still standing on the bridge.

subject: Sequoia
fact: Sequoia is a rogue who observes the environment, notices foot traffic leading to the door, deduces Zephyr’s illusion, leads the team through the bandit chamber, kills multiple bandits, blocks the exit, and comforts Voss after Calmer’s terrifying explanation; he rolls his eyes at Calmer’s fear and takes initiative.
source_quote: Sequoia examines the ground and whispers, “The foot traffic goes to the door.” “Zephyr has used an illusion to get the folks inside to open the door for us,” thinks Sequoia. Sequoia can see the cleric’s fear and rolls his eyes — “Zephyr, let’s go.” Sequoia kills one with his shortswords and then leaves the chamber. Sequoia kills one more of the bandits and then stands in front of the exit, blocking it. Sequoia pushes the cleric away and sits down next to Voss. He says, “Look, I know you are just a desperate man caught up in something bigger than themselves. And I really don’t need to hand you over to the authorities. I just need to know what this symbol is.”

subject: Thrune
fact: Thrune is a Tiefling who shouts that the party will die before making it through the door; he suggests cooking frog legs and says they taste like chicken; he mocks the group’s progress and asks if they are calling it quits.
source_quote: So you guys going to die before you even make it through the door,” shouts Thrune. Thurne shouts, “I can cook something nice with those legs. Tastes like chicken.” Thrune can’t resist, “So are we calling it quits?”
